methods.description: Find a base face diagonal using Pythagoras, keep it exact, then use it with a perpendicular edge to find the space diagonal. Exact answers, decimal answers, cubes and longest rods use this same method.

examples.derivation: In right-angled triangle ABC, AC² = 8² + 6² = 100, so AC = 10 cm exactly. In right-angled triangle ACG, AG² = 10² + 5² = 125, so AG = √125 cm ≈ 11.18 cm. The corner-to-opposite-corner diagonal gives the longest rod. This follows the source's two-triangle method, retaining the exact intermediate length.

For cube edge a, AC² = 2a² and AG² = AC² + a² = 3a². With AG = 18 cm, 324 = 3a², hence a² = 108 and a = √108 cm. Volume = 108√108 ≈ 1122.3689 cm³, giving 1122.4 cm³ to 1 decimal place. Surface area = 6 × 108 = 648 cm². The reverse-diagonal task is supported by source Mastery Q9.
